question: Who is the Chairperson of the 16th Finance Commission of India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Arvind Panagariya**__**.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **N. K. Singh** was the Chairperson of the **15th Finance Commission** and is a notable economist and policymaker in India.
 
• The **16th Finance Commission** has been constituted as of the latest updates. The Chairperson of the 16th Finance Commission of India is Dr. Arvind Panagariya. 
 
• The Chairperson of a Finance Commission is typically an expert in public finance, economics, or administration, ensuring that the recommendations align with national priorities.
 
• **N. K. Singh**, as the Chairperson of the 15th Finance Commission, played a significant role in addressing critical financial issues such as **tax devolution, grants to local bodies, and disaster management funds.**
 
• The Finance Commission is a constitutional body established under **Article 280 of the Indian Constitution**, which ensures a sound fiscal relationship between the **Union and the States.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **About the Finance Commission:**

 
 
• The Finance Commission is a **constitutional body** constituted by the President of India every **five years** under **Article 280**.
 
• Its primary function is to recommend the division of **tax revenues** between the **Union and the States** and among the states themselves.
 
• It also addresses issues related to **grants-in-aid** for local bodies and other financial matters as referred to it by the President.
 
 
 
• **Key Responsibilities of the Chairperson:**
 
 
• To lead discussions on **fiscal policies** and ensure equitable revenue sharing between the Union and States.
 
• To analyze and address economic challenges, such as **fiscal deficits, state debts, and revenue mobilization.**
 
• To guide the Commission in providing recommendations for financial governance and intergovernmental fiscal relations.
 
 
 
• **About N. K. Singh:**
 
 
• Nand Kishore Singh is a prominent Indian economist, policymaker, and former IAS officer.
 
• He has held key positions, including **Revenue Secretary** and **Expenditure Secretary** in the Government of India.
 
• As Chairperson of the 15th Finance Commission, he addressed vital issues such as **vertical and horizontal tax devolution, local body finances, and disaster management funds.**
 
 
 
• **Article 280 of the Constitution:**
 
 
• This Article mandates the formation of the Finance Commission by the President every five years or earlier, as required.
 
• The Commission consists of a **Chairperson** and four other members appointed by the President.
 
• Its recommendations are advisory, but they carry significant weight in shaping fiscal policies and governance.
 
 
 
• **Historical Background:**
 
 
• The first Finance Commission was constituted in **1951** under the Chairmanship of **K.C. Neogy**.
 
• Since then, 15 Finance Commissions have been constituted, addressing India's evolving fiscal needs and governance challenges.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **15th Finance Commission Recommendations:**

 
 
• Vertical devolution of **41% of the divisible tax pool** to states, a reduction from 42% due to Jammu & Kashmir's reorganization.
 
• Special grants and performance-based incentives for states to improve governance and fiscal management.
 
• Focus on **health, education, and disaster risk management** in fiscal transfers.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Finance Commissions:**
 
 
• They ensure a balanced fiscal relationship between **different levels of government.**
 
• They promote financial stability and equitable development across regions in India.
 
• They help address fiscal challenges like **debt sustainability and resource mobilization** in a growing economy.
